outcome: Clinical manifestations of SSI (purulent discharge, fever, local pain, induration, spontaneous superficial dehiscence, wound opening)
Causative microorganisms of SSI (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Escherichia coli)
cohort: The study examined 800 instances of lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) performed over a two-year period.
finding: The prevalence of surgical site infection (SSI) after caesarean delivery was 6.25%, with Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) being identified as the most prevalent microorganism.
mod_finding: A prevalence of 6.25% for surgical site infection was observed following caesarean delivery.
